subject: SLA exception request: automatic failback & version anchoring for HelixHealth canary
messages:
From: Emma Torres <emma@helixhealth.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 9 Feb 2026 15:13:00 -0800
Subject: Request: SLA pin & rapid failback during phased rollout

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're targeting a limited production canary for HelixHealth on March 2 — A/B traffic with roughly 10% routed to Redwood for inference. Our security and procurement teams flagged the need for a formal SLA exception that guarantees rapid automatic fallback and a version anchoring mechanism if latency or error rates regress.

Essential asks from our side:
- Automatic fallback to a known-good model/version if p95 latency > 450ms for 5m or error rate > 1% for the same window.
- Option to pin traffic to a stable version for a rolling window while we complete verification.
- A short playbook and closing checklist for operations to reference during the canary.

I attached the draft deployment plan (helix_canary_plan_v1.xlsx). Can you confirm whether Redwood can support the triggers above and provide a one-page exception form for our procurement team?

Appreciate it — Emma
Emma Torres
Director, Engineering
HelixHealth

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Torres <emma@helixhealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 9 Feb 2026 16:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: SLA pin & rapid failback during phased rollout

Emma —

Thanks for the clear ask and for sharing the plan. Short answer: yes, we can support both automatic failback and version anchoring as part of a documented SLA exception for a controlled canary. I've attached a draft of our autofallback playbook (autofallback_playbook.pdf) and a blank SLA exception template (sla-exception-form.docx).

Proposed automatic triggers (recommendation):
- Error-rate trigger: 1.0% 5m rolling
- Latency trigger: p95 > 500ms 5m rolling (we can lower to 450ms but that increases false positives in noisy regions)
- Unrecoverable errors (5xx spike or model OOM): immediate failback

Failback behavior:
- Immediate routing to the pinned stable variant + an alert to on-call + rollback ticket auto-created in Jira (link below).
- Lock the canary traffic split (no further expansion) until manual signoff.

Next steps:
1) Do you want the stricter 450ms threshold, or would you prefer we pilot at 500ms and tighten after 24h of telemetry?
2) I'll loop in Hannah for formal approval of the SLA carveout and Marcus for infra readiness.

Proposed meeting times attached.

—So
So-Jean (Soojin) Lee
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Agree with the approach, but a couple of notes from product:
- p95 500ms is more realistic at initial launch across multi-AZ; 450ms will flag transient infra jitter. Recommend 500ms for the first 48h and then reassess.
- For the pinned-version flow, we need a clear TTL on the pin (suggest 72h) after which it expires unless extended via console or API.
- We should include a read-only dashboard share to Helix for the canary window so they can see the triggers in near real-time.

I'll help codify the thresholds into the exception form.

karthik

Redwood Inference

- Explicit evidence of automatic failback behavior during simulated faults (playback logs or runbook excerpt).

We're happy to accept 500ms for pilot if it's documented and we get visibility into the dashboard and ops alerts. I've shared a DocuSign envelope for the SoW with my legal team; they also asked for the SLA carveout as an addendum.

Subject: SLA carveout approval request — HelixHealth canary (summary + mitigation)

Hannah —

Quick summary and ask: HelixHealth is scheduling an A/B canary with Redwood on 2026-03-02. Procurement requires a formal carveout that documents automatic failback, version pinning, and expected failback latency. Key points:
- Proposed triggers: 1% error-rate (5m), p95 latency > 500ms (5m), immediate for 5xx surge/OOM.
- Failback behavior: immediate routing to pinned stable variant; auto-creation of rollback ticket; alert to on-call. Target mean route-complete for failback: <= 90s.
- TTL on pins: 72h unless extended.
- Customer wants dashboard share and playbook excerpt — attached.

Attachments: autofallback_playbook.pdf, sla-exception-form.docx, helix_canary_plan_v1.xlsx

Request: approve SLA carveout for a controlled pilot with the thresholds above (we will tighten after initial telemetry). Once approved I'll finalize the addendum and coordinate with legal/procurement on the DocuSign envelope.

Thanks — Soojin
